text.p: These are the headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Dingwall softening on tobacco bill: Delaying rules on industry sponsorship of sports, art events an option, minister says.
- Chretien attacked over integrity: Reform, Bloc see potential issue.
- Leach rules out alterations in merger: Minister open to 'minor' changes.
- Sharif sweeps to victory in Pakistani election: Low voter turnout jeopardizes hopes of stability for new government.
- Mandela gets praise, asks for investment: Business seen to be ignoring Africa.
- Infection experts alarmed by drug-resistant bacteria: Hospitals fear deadly complications in some cases.
- Precision Drilling bids for rival: Oil services firm may follow hostile C$410-million offer for Kenting with play for Lynx.
- Death, controversy become him: Analyst Steven Saltzman isn't retreating from his views on Loewen Group - even if it means feuding with Ray Loewen.
- Martin sets Feb. 18 for budget: Will resist push to crank up spending.
- Bre-X doesn't own Busang: Indonesia: Official questions stake in gold find.
- Precision Drilling makes lightning bid for Kenting: Newly-born oil-rig firm tries to fend off C$431-million offer with link to Lynx Energy.
- B.C. stalls new interprovincial trade deal.
